title: free-disk-space journeys
description: A developer's way through the tool as its README orders the commands and as each command's closing lines point to the next.

entities.name: Reclaim disk space, then keep it
entities.description: From a nearly full disk to a Mac that cleans up after itself: quick cleanups first, then the slower scan, dedupe and compression, then the background daemon.
entities.goal: Get space back on their Mac without losing anything they need, and not run out again.

stages.touchpoint: Homebrew (the zazzle formula), the zazzle release tarball or a cargo build
stages.action: Installs free-disk-space, which comes with the other toolbox binaries; after a browser download of an unsigned build, removes the quarantine attribute.
stages.outcome: free-disk-space --help lists the commands and examples.

stages.context: Wants to know what is safe to delete before deleting anything.
stages.outcome: Per folder and per artifact, what would go, its size and the running total, the dev artifacts kept or uncertain, and `Nothing was changed. Re-run with --apply.`

stages.action: Applies the cleanup to the targets they accept.
stages.outcome: Space freed, with a running total of what is deleted, the actual free-space change beside the summed sizes, and a pointer to new and compress for more. If they stop it with Ctrl-C, the next applying clean within 12 hours skips what was already done.

stages.context: Wants more space; the scan can take long, so it may span several sittings.
stages.action: Starts a scan of their home, stops it with Ctrl-C when they need the machine, and resumes it later.
stages.outcome: `Scan complete` with the candidates and estimated saving, and the next steps: dedupe to preview cloning, list and compress --sample 5.

stages.context: Before compressing, since compressed files cannot be deduped.
stages.action: Previews the duplicates, applies cloning to a sample of 5, checks those files and the free-space change, then applies it to the rest.
stages.outcome: Identical copies share their blocks; the report gives the upper bound on savings and the actual change.

stages.context: Wants old, large files to take less space.
stages.action: Compresses a sample of 5 and compares the verified saving with the free-space change, then compresses up to a limit with --yes.
stages.outcome: `Sample finished. If it looks right, run compress without --sample.`, then the larger run's verified saving and how many files were skipped for each reason. Where ditto --hfsCompression does not really compress (macOS 26/27), compress stops before changing anything.

stages.context: Does not want to do this by hand again.
stages.touchpoint: free-disk-space daemon install, and later daemon status and the log
stages.action: Installs the daemon with the targets it may clean, and checks on it now and then.
stages.outcome: Caches and old build output are cleared whenever free space drops below the threshold while the Mac is in use.

relatedViews.relationship: The use cases behind the cleanup, compress, dedupe and automate stages.
